help.intro: Rents, prices of bikes and phones, distances, the year you were born: from here on the numbers get long, and German writes them as one word — 650 is sechshundertfünfzig, 1.200 is tausendzweihundert. The good news is that nothing new is hidden inside them. You say the hundreds, then the last two digits exactly as you learnt them, with the unit first: 385 = dreihundert-fünfundachtzig. Thousands work the same way: 8.500 = achttausend-fünfhundert. Two things are different from English. First, German marks thousands with a full stop and decimals with a comma: 1.200 means twelve hundred, 1,20 means one point two. Second, years before 2000 are said in hundreds: 1998 is neunzehnhundertachtundneunzig, never 'tausendneunhundert…'; from 2000 on you say zweitausend: 2020 = zweitausendzwanzig.
help.tips[0].title: Hundreds + the number you already know
help.tips[0].text: Say how many hundreds, then the last two digits the German way (unit + und + ten). All of it is one word; ein before hundert and tausend is optional.
help.tips[0].trap: Do not insert spaces or an extra und after hundert: sechshundertfünfzig, not "sechshundert und fünfzig".
help.tips[0].check.why: Say the hundreds, then the last two digits, all as one word with no extra und after hundert.
help.tips[1].title: Thousands: the full stop is not a decimal point
help.tips[1].text: 1.200 = tausendzweihundert (also zwölfhundert). 8.500 = achttausendfünfhundert. 20.000 = zwanzigtausend. A comma is the decimal point: 1,5 Kilo = one and a half kilos.
help.tips[1].trap: In English 1.200 is 'one point two'. In German it is twelve hundred.
help.tips[1].check.q: A German sign says: 2.500 Einwohner. How many people live there?
help.tips[1].check.why: In German the full stop marks thousands: 2.500 = zweitausendfünfhundert. The decimal point is a comma.
help.tips[2].title: Years: hundreds before 2000, zweitausend after
help.tips[2].text: 1965 = neunzehnhundertfünfundsechzig. 1998 = neunzehnhundertachtundneunzig. 2020 = zweitausendzwanzig. And a year stands alone: Ich bin 1998 geboren — no in.
help.tips[2].check.why: Years before 2000 are said in hundreds (neunzehnhundert…), and the year stands alone without in.
help.tips[3].title: Read from the left, flip the last two
help.tips[3].text: Take 585: fünfhundert (left) + fünfundachtzig (flip the 8 and the 5). Only the last pair is ever flipped.
help.tips[3].check.why: Read the hundreds from the left (dreihundert), then flip only the last pair: 76 = sechsundsiebzig.
help.tips[4].title: Ordinal numbers: -te up to 19, -ste from 20
help.tips[4].text: Dates and rankings use ordinals, written with a full stop: der 1. Mai = der erste Mai. Add -te to the numbers 2 to 19 (zweite, vierte, zehnte, neunzehnte) and -ste from 20 upwards (zwanzigste, dreißigste, hundertste). Three are irregular: erste, dritte, siebte.
help.tips[4].examples[0].en: Today is the first of May.
help.tips[4].examples[1].en: Tomorrow is the third of June.
help.tips[4].examples[2].en: The thirty-first of December is New Year’s Eve.
help.tips[4].trap: The full stop after the figure is the ordinal mark: 3. Juni reads dritte Juni, never drei Juni.
help.remember[0]: One number, one word: sechshundertfünfzig, tausendzweihundert.
help.remember[1]: Years before 2000 in hundreds (neunzehnhundert…), after 2000 with zweitausend.
help.remember[2]: Ordinals: -te to 19, -ste from 20; erste, dritte, siebte are irregular. 3. Juni = dritte Juni.
help.context.en: The flat has two rooms and costs 980 euros a month. The house is old – it is from 1912. It is only twelve kilometres to work, and the bike costs 199 euros.
help.mistakes[0].why: The whole number is one word, and there is no und after hundert.
help.mistakes[1].why: Years before 2000 are said in hundreds.
help.mistakes[2].why: The full stop groups thousands; the comma is the decimal point.
help.hook: Rent, bikes, birth years: big German numbers are just the small ones you know, glued into one long word.
sentences[0].english: The flat costs 650 euros a month.
sentences[0].why: Hundreds stack up front: sechs·hundert, then fünfzig — all one word, no 'and' after the hundred.
sentences[1].why: hundert, then units before tens: neun·und·neunzig — 'nine-and-ninety'.
sentences[2].why: A round hundred is just the digit + hundert: dreihundert.
sentences[3].english: My hotel room has the number 112.
sentences[3].why: hundert + zwölf — 13 to 19 and the teens keep their own words, so no swapping here.
sentences[4].english: It is 585 kilometres from Berlin to Munich.
sentences[5].why: vierhundert + sechzehn — sechzehn is a teen word, said as is (and it clips sechs to sech-).
sentences[6].why: neunhundert + achtzig — a plain ten needs no swap: achtzig.
sentences[7].why: hundert + zwanzig; the ein- in front of hundert is optional.
sentences[8].english: The train goes 250 kilometres an hour.
sentences[8].why: zweihundert + fünfzig — hundreds first, then the rest, one word.
sentences[9].why: tausend + zweihundert; German can also say zwölfhundert, 'twelve hundred'.
sentences[10].why: acht·tausend·fünf·hundert — thousands, then hundreds, all one word.
sentences[11].why: zwanzig·tausend — say the 20, then tausend; big numbers chain the same way.
sentences[12].why: Years before 2000 are said in hundreds: neunzehn·hundert + achtundneunzig — 'nineteen hundred…'.
sentences[13].why: neunzehnhundert + fünf·und·sechzig — hundreds for the year, units before tens.
sentences[14].why: From 2000 on, years are plain numbers: zweitausend·zwanzig — no hundreds trick.
sentences[15].why: zweitausendvierhundert — or vierundzwanzighundert, 'twenty-four hundred', like in English.
sentences[16].why: neunzehnhundert + sieben·und·dreißig — the year in hundreds, units before tens.
sentences[17].why: tausend·dreihundert + neunundneunzig — units before tens close the number.
sentences[18].english: I have lived in Cologne since 2008.
sentences[19].english: Today is the first of May.
sentences[19].why: Dates take ordinals; 'first' is irregular: der erste — not einte.
sentences[20].english: Tomorrow is the third of June.
sentences[20].why: 'Third' is irregular: der dritte — not dreite.
sentences[21].english: The seventh day of the week is Sunday.
sentences[21].why: Ordinals to 19 add -te; sieben clips to siebte.
sentences[22].english: Today is the twentieth of October.
sentences[22].why: From 20 up, ordinals add -ste: der zwanzigste.
sentences[23].english: The thirty-first of December is New Year’s Eve.
sentences[23].why: einunddreißig + -ste = der einunddreißigste — big ordinals take -ste.
